newsitem.title: USA: Girl cleared in Florida vampire cult murders.
newsitem.headline: Girl cleared in Florida vampire cult murders.

text.p: A Florida grand jury on Tuesday cleared a 15-year-old girl of charges that she helped a vampire cult that allegedly murdered her parents.

Heather Wendorf was freed after the jury found "no probable cause" to prosecute her for the murder of her parents, Richard and Ruth Wendorf, who were slain in their Eustis, Florida, home on Nov. 25, State Attorney Brad King said.

Rod Ferrell, Scott Anderson and Charity Kessee, all 16, and Dana Lynn Cooper, 19, were indicted for the murders in December. All four are being treated as adults in the case and could face the death penalty if convicted.
Wendorf was not indicted, but was being held in a detention centre under a juvenile murder charge.

The state claims that Ferrell, the alleged ringleader of a Kentucky "vampire clan" who drank one another's blood and engaged in bizarre rituals, killed the Wendorfs with a crowbar or a claw hammer and that the other three youths helped to plan and execute the murder.

After the Wendorfs were killed, the five teenagers disappeared and police say they drove to New Orleans and Baton Rouge before running short of money. Kessee phoned her mother and that led police to the group on Nov. 28.
Wendorf's lawyer, James Hope, said Tuesday's jury decision showed his client had in fact been through a frightening ordeal.

"For some 60 days the whole world thought she was a murderess," Hope said. "Now we have a finding of no probable cause. We have witnesses who have recanted, witnesses who are unreliable. This is the truth that Heather knew would come out."
The trial of the other four defendants, all originally from Kentucky, is tentatively scheduled to begin in September.
